clue.text: Privileged choice blighting showjumper's debut?

definitions.meaning: the right to be offered something before anyone else, a preferential option
a horse balking at the opening fence of its round, spoiling the start

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the contractual option to buy before others; the other is a horse's opening balk at a jump.

clue.text: When one is presumably not slow to suspend courses?

definitions.text: When one is presumably not slow to suspend courses?

parts.words: When one is presumably not slow to suspend courses?
parts.note: read 'not slow' as quick in pace, but the real sense is a period of abstaining, suspending the courses of meals

explanation.definitionFit: A religious day of abstinence is a time when meal courses are suspended, and its first word also means quick.

clue.text: Talked incessantly about work in old Asian city

indicators.note: the phrase for chattering on is placed around the word for work, enclosing it

parts.note: ran on means kept talking without stopping
go means work or function, as a machine does

explanation.surface: Someone chattered endlessly about a job in an old Burmese city.
explanation.definitionFit: The former name of Yangon, Myanmar's largest city, so an Asian city of old.

clue.text: Display extravagant paintings all over restaurant

indicators.note: means the whole run of pieces is turned over, read from the end back to the start

parts.note: to air something is to display it
OTT is short for over the top, extravagant
art means paintings collectively

explanation.surface: An eatery shows off its lavish pictures on every wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' turns AIROTTART round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian-style eating house, a type of restaurant.

clue.text: Former partner writing about a summer term commitment?

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or lover
MS is manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: An ex-husband writes about committing to something for the summer term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here just links the writing to its subject, A; the question mark flags that tests fill the summer term in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Tests sat at the end of the school year are what pupils commit to in the summer term.

clue.text: Rebuke bachelor originally in court over assault

indicators.note: the bachelor's opening letter goes inside the combined court and assault pieces
in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: to be up is to appear before a court
a raid is an assault or attack

indicators.note: signals the opening letter of bachelor only

explanation.surface: A single man first appears in court for an assault and is told off.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the court piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold someone severely; a synonym of rebuke as a verb.

clue.text: Not many, possibly? It means the opposite

indicators.note: suggests the letters might be arranged some other way, an anagram

explanation.surface: Asked if 'not many' is right, someone says the word means the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges NOTMANY.
explanation.definitionFit: A word with the opposite meaning to another, exactly what this term describes.

clue.text: Lowest degree university's given —- Bill may receive it

parts.note: a third is the lowest class of British honours degree
Reading is an English university town; the 's is read as 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A graduate with the poorest grade gets a university place.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a third-class honours is the bottom grade; Reading is a university in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary bill goes through a final debating stage in the chamber with this name before passing.

clue.text: Cry of praise from woman with religious book

parts.note: Hos is the abbreviation of Hosea, a book of the Bible
Anna is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman holding a Bible shouts in praise.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of adoration used in Christian and Jewish worship, an acclamation of God.

clue.text: Shrub only found in Arkansas, America

indicators.note: the word for only is placed within the abbreviations for the US state and nation

parts.note: AR is the postal abbreviation for Arkansas
US is the United States, America
but means only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: A bush grows nowhere but in one southern American state.
explanation.definitionFit: The strawberry tree genus, an evergreen bush, so a kind of shrub.

clue.text: Player's attendant given racket

definitions.note: the possessive is read as 'Player is', the definition naming a performer

parts.note: a second attends a boxer or duellist
a fiddle is a swindle or racket

explanation.surface: A sports star's helper gets involved in a scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player's' reads as 'Player is': the answer is a player, a violinist in the second section.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a violinist of the second section of an orchestra, so a player; figuratively a subordinate.

clue.text: Soldier put on by revelling painters in town?

definitions.meaning: a British infantryman of old, named for the scarlet tunic

definitions.text: put on by revelling painters in town?
definitions.meaning: people out partying are said to paint the town red, so they would apply a scarlet layer of paint

explanation.walkthrough: To 'paint the town red' is a British idiom for a wild night out.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic British troops wore scarlet jackets; the second reading is a scarlet layer of paint applied by those painting the town.

clue.text: Tin cans unexpectedly containing tin

indicators.note: signals the letters of the two words turn up in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: Food cans turn out to be made of the metal after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges TINCANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry adjective for compounds of tin in its higher valency, from Latin stannum.

clue.text: Fellow being shown textile fibre

parts.note: Ray is a man's name, a fellow
on means showing, as a film is on

explanation.surface: A man is demonstrating a fabric material.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial silk made from cellulose, a man-made textile fibre.

clue.text: He delivers sliced bread to west of island

indicators.note: in an across clue the bread piece sits on the left, westward, of the island

parts.note: a round is a slice or sandwich of bread
Man is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A man brings sandwiches to the western side of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: A round of bread is a British term for a slice or sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who makes regular delivery rounds, such as a milkman, is one who delivers.

clue.text: Way padre is represented in a French ship?

indicators.note: the rearranged clergyman goes inside the French article and the ship

parts.note: un is French for a
SS is steamship

indicators.note: the letters of the word are presented in a different form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A chaplain is depicted aboard a French vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is represented' rearranges the clergyman's five letters to DERPA.
explanation.definitionFit: A road or path running beneath another road, a way through.

clue.text: Ideas for a novel previously referred to

indicators.note: new or different, telling us to make a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone has thoughts for a book that were mentioned earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but signals rearranging IDEASFORA.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal legal word meaning mentioned earlier in the same document.

clue.text: Eponymous hero's extremely offbeat greeting

definitions.note: the possessive is read as 'hero is', a link

indicators.note: takes only the extreme letters, first and last, of offbeat

parts.note: hello is a greeting

explanation.surface: A title character has an unusual way of saying hi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of offbeat, O and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Moor gives his name to the play, the eponymous tragic hero.

clue.text: Charm originally obtained in eastern part of Belgium

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east

indicators.note: the opening letter is put inside the combined eastern and Belgian pieces

parts.note: Namur is a Belgian province and city

indicators.note: signals the first letter of obtained

explanation.surface: A charm was first acquired in the east of Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives O, which 'in' puts inside E plus NAMUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate or delight someone, a synonym of charm as a verb.

clue.text: Runner following fellow in boat

parts.note: a ski is a runner, as on a sledge
f is the abbreviation for following, as in pp 6f

explanation.surface: A racer pursues a man in a small craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete but is a sledge runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A light rowing or sculling vessel, a small boat.

clue.text: Put up a chap with soldier's wife on the Continent

indicators.note: in a down clue this lifts the run of pieces so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Ron is a man's name
GIs are American soldiers; the soldier's becomes the plural

explanation.surface: Someone lodges a man with an army officer's wife in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' turns ARONGIS upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian title for a married woman, so a wife in continental Europe.

clue.text: List cohabitants beginning to settle in one quarter

parts.note: an item is a couple in a relationship

indicators.note: the first letter of settle goes inside the one and quarter pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
E is east, a quarter of the compass

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of settle

explanation.surface: A couple living together start settling in one part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' gives S, which 'in' puts between I and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out things one by one; to list as a verb.

clue.text: Somewhat lame, maladjusted son of Abraham?

parts.note: the suffix -ish means somewhat

indicators.note: badly adjusted, so the letters of lame are set wrongly

explanation.surface: Abraham's son was a bit lame and poorly adjusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maladjusted' rearranges LAME to MAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Abraham's elder son by Hagar; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Start off without a meal

indicators.note: means the word for starting off loses the a

parts.note: to launch is to start something off

explanation.surface: Someone sets off without eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A from LAUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: The midday meal, one of the day's meals.

clue.text: Threat to horses you and I raved about

indicators.note: the word for raved goes around the pronoun

parts.note: raged means raved, ranted wildly
we is you and I together

explanation.surface: Two people shouted angrily about a danger to horses.
explanation.walkthrough: Ragweed (ragwort) is poisonous to grazing horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed poisonous to livestock, so a danger to grazing horses.

clue.text: Young female diver makes binding for dress

parts.note: a gal is a girl, a young female
the loon is a diving bird, called a diver in Britain

explanation.surface: A girl who dives produces trimming for a gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow braid or ribbon trimming used to edge clothing, a binding on a dress.

clue.text: A note about spies lacking friendly instincts

indicators.note: the musical note goes around the spy agency

parts.note: sol is a note of the sol-fa scale
the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: A musical note on the subject of spies who are unsociable.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoiding the company of others; not sociable in temperament.

clue.text: Press for civil power to protect university

indicators.note: the outer pieces enclose the university letter, guarding it

parts.note: taken as written
the state is the civil power of government

explanation.surface: Someone lobbies for government power to defend a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' puts U inside FOR, giving FOUR before THE STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalism collectively, regarded as a fourth power alongside the traditional estates of the realm.
